EXP003:candidate-v3:procedure.source_text: After the switch returns to its centre position, push it inward to cancel. The manual shows left ON, centre push OFF and right ON.

EXP005:candidate-v3:procedure.source_text: Use the Home button on the left-hand handlebar control; the manual describes it as the go-back control.

EXP006:candidate-v3:procedure.source_text: The manual says brightness can be adjusted only in dark theme. Press joystick UP to display Settings. Highlight Appearance with joystick up/down and centre-press to open it. Highlight Background and centre-press; highlight Dark Theme using up/down and centre-press to select. Use Home to return to Appearance, highlight Brightness and centre-press: joystick right increases brightness; left decreases it. Use Home to go back. Make menu changes while stopped safely (product policy).

EXP008:candidate-v3:procedure.source_text: While safely stopped (product policy), press joystick UP to open Settings. Highlight Trip Preference using up/down and centre-press to open it. Highlight Reset Trip and centre-press. Highlight Reset Trip1 with up/down and centre-press. The display asks for confirmation; confirm only if you intend to reset that trip, or decline. Home returns to the previous screen.

EXP012:candidate-v3:procedure.source_text: The manual says not to release the brake lever/pedal when pulsations occur during hard braking in an emergency; these indicate ABS activation. Apply both brakes simultaneously. ABS does not substitute for careful riding or anticipation and does not reduce braking distance; in some circumstances it can lengthen it. Ride and brake carefully, especially while cornering. Anticipate the stopping distance for your speed and brake well in advance. The instrument cluster must function properly as it is integral to ABS. Failing to follow these cautions can cause an accident with serious injury or loss of life.

EXP015:candidate-v3:procedure.source_text: The manual describes roll-over-sensor shutdown in that situation. Before its reset, the bike must be safely upright on its centre stand on firm flat ground, in neutral with the neutral lamp glowing. Take extreme care: a fall can injure you or others and damage the bike. Only do this once the motorcycle is already securely supported. The reset guidance does not provide instructions for lifting a fallen bike or safely placing it on the stand. If you can safely confirm those conditions, switch both ignition and stop switches OFF, wait a few seconds, then switch them ON. This does not establish that the bike is undamaged or safe to ride; if condition after the fall is uncertain, have authorised service inspect it.

EXP017:candidate-v3:procedure.source_text: On firm flat ground, hold the handlebar firmly straight, lower the centre stand until both legs rest on firm ground, apply pressure to its fulcrum lever and pull the motorcycle backward. Lock steering and ensure the handlebar is firmly locked before removing the key. Exercise extreme care: a fall can injure people and damage the bike. Retract both stands before riding.

EXP025:candidate-v3:procedure.source_text: Place the bike upright on a firm level surface and ensure the rear reservoir is horizontal. Check that fluid lies between MAX and Min. Insufficient brake fluid can cause brake-system failure.

a_cool_engine:candidate-v3:procedure.source_text: Switch the engine OFF and allow it to cool. The manual does not specify a cooling time or temperature at which restarting is safe. If unsure, have an authorised Royal Enfield service centre assess it. Apply this high-level branch only when its documented condition is established; no unsupported temperature threshold may establish eligibility.

a_fuse:candidate-v3:procedure.source_text: With ignition OFF, replace only a defective, positively identified fuse with a new fuse of the same specified rating. Do not guess the circuit or rating from colour alone. After any fuse failure, have the electrical system thoroughly checked and faults corrected immediately at authorised service, even if replacement restores operation. Never bridge a defective fuse or substitute conductive material; this risks short-circuit and fire. Wrong-rating or low-grade fuses can damage the electrical system. Replenish a used spare fuse in its holder at the earliest opportunity. Keep ignition OFF for fuse work. Circuit, rating and defective condition must be established; uncertainty in condition goes directly to service.

a_raise_stand:candidate-v3:procedure.source_text: Fully retract the side stand before starting or moving. The manual describes the stand cutoff as stopping the engine when gear is engaged for rider safety. Confirm the actual stand position and reported indicator condition; a discrepancy is not a sensor diagnosis.

a_refuel:candidate-v3:procedure.source_text: Read the guidance before refuelling and return to the chat after completion. Open the fuel cap slowly and top up only to the bottom of the anti-splash plate, leaving expansion space; do not fill to the brim. Gasoline vapour is highly explosive; no smoking, flames or sparks while refuelling or while the cap is open. Overfilling can send gasoline into the EVAP canister and damage the emission system. Avoid fuel spills on painted surfaces and wipe any immediately to prevent permanent stains. Refuel only with engine OFF in a well-ventilated area, no smoking/flames/sparks and mobile/handheld devices OFF. Read beforehand and return to chat after completion. Press the cap to lock with the key in position, then remove the key and close the flap.

a_switches_on:candidate-v3:procedure.source_text: Set only the reported OFF ignition or engine kill switch to the documented ON or RUN position. This does not establish that the remaining starting conditions are satisfied. When finishing checks with the engine not running, turn ignition OFF; the continuously ON headlamp can discharge the battery. Setting a switch does not authorize starting. Establish the compact starting checklist before any starter action; retained confirmations are not re-asked.
